Subject: Lockstep MAP: evaluation milestones => MSA/DPA/Order Form dependencies

Hi Danielle —

Following our call this morning, attaching a concise MAP that ties the evaluation milestones to the contracting handoffs. The goal here is to keep the pilot acceptance gating (test dataset run + latency/throughput checks) separate from the legal signoffs so we don’t block go/no-go technical work while procurement completes the MSA/DPA/order form path.

Key ask: can procurement confirm whether Novacare requires the signed MSA before purchase order issuance, or if a commercial PO is acceptable to kick off Dedicated capacity procurement while legal finalizes the DPA? That determines whether we open the order form now or wait for signature.

Quick summary of the MAP (high level):
- Week 0 (6/21): Pilot kickoff, infra provisioning in our Dedicated pool (temporary resource tags) — tech can start smoke tests.
- Week 2 (7/05): Eval milestone A — model accuracy/throughput report (Redwood to deliver). If green, Redwood will prepare OrderForm Draft v1.
- Week 3 (7/12): Procurement window — Novacare confirms PO vs signed MSA requirement.
- Week 4 (7/19): Legal review of DPA clauses that touch processing scope & data residency (Laura leading for Redwood).
- Week 6 (7/31): Target signature window (MSA + DPA + OrderForm) — contingent on procurement path.

Attached: Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx (milestone table), DPA_clause_summary.docx (our suggested redlines), OrderForm_Draft_v1.pdf (commercial terms stub).

If procurement can accept a PO to provision capacity we’ll mark the order form as 'commercial in progress' and proceed with pilot scale tests. If MSA signature is hard requirement, please flag the blockers and Laura and I will prioritize the DPA redline turnaround.

Thanks —
David

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Lockstep MAP: evaluation milestones => MSA/DPA/Order Form dependencies

David —

Thanks for the clear map and attachments. Two questions from procurement:
1) Novacare standard practice is to issue a commercial PO if the vendor can accept our standard terms on the order form and the MSA is still being circulated. But for vendors handling PHI-adjacent data we usually require the DPA in place before any production data flows. Our pilot will use de‑identified test sets, so procurement may be comfortable with a PO to provision capacity on the condition that no production data or PHI is used until DPA is executed.
2) Who on Redwood will own the DPA redline turnaround? We have a tight window and would like to avoid legal churn.

Procurement has a holiday blackout week starting 7/06–7/09; best to have the PO ready before that if possible.

—Danielle
Danielle Moore
Director, Clinical Integrations | Novacare Health
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Danielle Moore <danielle.moore@novacarehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lockstep MAP: evaluation milestones => MSA/DPA/Order Form dependencies

Thanks Danielle — that helps. Confirming Redwood position:
- We are comfortable with a PO to provision Dedicated capacity as long as the PO explicitly limits the scope to 'pilot/test data only' and prohibits production PHI until a DPA is signed. We will not ingest production data without the executed DPA.
- Laura Bennett (cc) will own Redwood's DPA redline turnaround and will work directly with your legal contact to minimize iterations. Laura — I’ve attached the DPA_clause_summary to this thread; it annotates items likely to draw questions (subprocessor list, data retention, incident response SLAs).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Danielle/procurement: confirm whether PO flow is acceptable and, if yes, provide PO template/PO number placeholder by 7/02 so we can provision ahead of your procurement blackout.
2) Laura & Novacare legal: exchange initial redlines this week; target 48–72 hour turnaround on each pass during this condensed window.
3) Monica & Rishi: coordinate technical gating — we’ll publish the eval checklist this afternoon so your team knows the pass/fail criteria for the Week 2 milestone.

Danielle, if that aligns I’ll update Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx to include a PO contingency lane and a compact DPA review cadence.

—David

Hi all —

Looping in with the DPA plan. I reviewed Danielle's note and the DPA_clause_summary. My approach:
- I’ll propose a focused redline set that limits negotiation to the few operationally critical items (data residency, subprocessors, and incident response). Everything else will remain in the commercial 'standard language' bucket to avoid broad renegotiation.
- Target: initial draft exchanged today (19 Jun) and aim for 1–2 business day turnaround on each pass. If Novacare can accept the PO gating approach described (PO for test/provisioning and explicit prohibition on production data), we can honor that.

Danielle — can you please share the preferred Novacare legal contact and a PO template (if you have one) so we can align the OrderForm_Draft_v1.pdf to your fields? If procurement can issue a preliminary PO number we’ll configure billing placeholders to speed activation.

Thanks —
